paragraphs.text: Here was aliud ex alio malum, one affliction on the neck of another. Matters mend with us as sour ale doth in summer, said Bishop Ridley once, when he was prisoner. Poor Jeremiah might well have said so, if ever any, as appeareth by this chapter, where we find him in a worse hole than was that of Jonathan; but his extremity was God’s opportunity.
paragraphs.anchor: Then Shephatiah.

paragraphs.text: These four princes here named to their eternal infamy were no small men, as appeareth in that the king was not he that could do anything against them. {Jer 38:5} The grandees of the world are greatest enemies usually to the truth. Little they had to say against his doctrines; they quarrel with his affection, as a perturber of the public peace. {Jer 38:4}
paragraphs.anchor: Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah, &c.

paragraphs.text: Ahab charged the like crime upon Elijah; the Jews upon Christ, and afterwards upon Paul; the heathen persecutors upon the primitive Christians; the heretics still upon the orthodox, that they were seditious, antimonarchical, &c.

This is the self-same truth which he had preached before, and for the which he suffered. See Jer 21:9. He is constant to his principles, and although it be commonly said and seen that he who receives a courtesy sells his liberty; yet it was not so with this holy prophet. He had received some enlargement, and care was taken by the king that a piece, or a roll of bread should be brought him daily to the prison out of the baker’s street: but that stoppeth not his mouth.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord, He that remaineth in the city.

paragraphs.text: And as long as the Lord saith so, I must say so too, whatever come of it. {Jer 1:9-10}
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Thus out of carnal policy is piety impugned. So 1Ki 12:27 Joh 11:48 Jer 38:1.
paragraphs.anchor: For thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war.

paragraphs.text: O nihil regem, qui ne verbulo quidem cruentis viris obluctatur! O king of clouts, saith one, who, knowing the prophet’s innocence and these princes’ blood thirstiness, durst not say a word for him or against them! This inconsistancy of his, and impotence of spirit, proceeded merely from diffidence and distrust in God.
paragraphs.anchor: Then Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand.

paragraphs.text: Whom the king had now (against his conscience, as afterwards Pilate dealt by Jesus), either through fear or favour, betrayed unto his deadly enemies; and so he was in a pitiful plight, in a forlorn condition. But Jeremiah, de profundis, out of the deep called upon God (whom he found far more facile than these princes did Zedekiah), "Thou drewest near," saith he, "in the day when I called upon thee; thou saidst, Fear not." {Lam 3:57} I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.
paragraphs.anchor: Then took they Jeremiah.

paragraphs.text: With a murderous intent there to make an end of him privily, ut ibi praefocatus moreretur; ille vero usque ad collum mersus ibi manebat, said Josephus, that he might there pine and perish; but God graciously prevented it.
paragraphs.anchor: And they let down Jeremiah with cords.

paragraphs.text: A typical hell it was, worse than Joseph’s pit, {Gen 37:24} or Heman’s lake, {Psa 88:6} or any prison that ever Brown the sect master ever came into, who used to boast that he had been committed to thirty-two prisons, and in some of them he could not see his hand at noonday. He died at length in Northampton jail, A.D. 1630, whereto he was sent for striking the constable requiring rudely the payment of a rate. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And in the dungeon there was no water but mire.

paragraphs.text: Up to the neck, saith Josephus, and so became a type of Christ. {Psa 69:2}
paragraphs.anchor: So Jeremiah sunk in the mire.

paragraphs.text: {a} Fuller’s Church Hist., 168.
But a proselyte, and a religious prince; a stranger, but (as that good Samaritan in the Gospel) more merciful than any of the Jewish nation, who gloried in their privileges. See Rom 2:26-27.
paragraphs.anchor: Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian.

paragraphs.text: And eunuchs, say the Rabbis, are ordinarily more cruel than other men; but so was not this Cushite. Piety is the fountain of all virtues whatsoever.
paragraphs.anchor: One of the eunuchs.

paragraphs.text: Which was in the king’s house.] As Obadiah was in Ahab’s, Nehemiah in Artaxerxes’s; some good people in Herod’s; {Luk 8:3} and Nero’s; {Php 4:22} Cromwell and Cranmer in Henry VIII’s.

Sitting in judgment, where Jeremiah’s enemies had once apprehended him for a fugitive, but durst not try it out with him, though Ebedmelech there entreated with the king for him in the presence of some of them, as it is probable.
paragraphs.anchor: The king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin.

paragraphs.text: Not more the king’s servant (so his name signifieth) than God’s. Joseph of Arimathea was such another, who went boldly to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus. Faith quelleth and killeth distrustful fear.
paragraphs.anchor: Ebedmelech.

paragraphs.text: What a brave man was this, to oppose so many princes, and so potent that the king himself dared not displease them! It was God’s holy Spirit that put this mettle into him, and gave him the freedom of speech. {Psa 119:46}
paragraphs.anchor: My lord the king, these men have done evil.

paragraphs.text: Or, Who would have died for hunger in the place where he was.
paragraphs.anchor: And he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is.

paragraphs.text: Cum panum annona sit pauca et parca. What need he to be doubly murdered?
paragraphs.anchor: For there is no more bread in the city.

paragraphs.text: A sweet providence of God thus to incline the heart of this effeminate, cruel, inconstant, and impious king, to hearken to the motion, and to give order for the prophet’s deliverance from that desperate and deadly danger. A good encouragement also to men to appear in a good cause, and to act vigorously for God, notwithstanding they are alone, and have to encounter with divers difficulties.
paragraphs.anchor: Then the king commanded Ebedmelech.

paragraphs.text: Four or fewer might have done it; but perhaps the princes with their forces might have endeavoured to hinder them, but that they saw them so strong.
paragraphs.anchor: Take from hence thirty men with thee.

paragraphs.text: The labour of love that this Ethiopian performed to the man of God is particularly and even partly described, for his eternal commendation, and all men’s imitation.
paragraphs.anchor: So Ebedmelech took the men with him and went.

paragraphs.text: Hence some gather that the prophet was put into this loathsome hole naked, or very ill clad at least. The fathers allegorise this story to set forth the vocaation of the Gentiles and the rejection of the Jews.
paragraphs.anchor: Put now these cast clouts.

paragraphs.text: And God was not unrighteous to forget this their work and labour of love. {Heb 6:10 Jer 39:17-18}
paragraphs.anchor: So they drew up Jeremiah with cords.

paragraphs.text: Manacled and fettered, as some {a} gather from Jer 40:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.

paragraphs.text: {a} R. David, Vatabl.

Then Zedekiah … took Jeremiah into the third entry.] Which was right over against the king’s house. This wretched king was so overawed by his counsellors that he dared not advise with God’s prophet in their presence, or with their privity.
It is for the sins of a people that a hypocrite reigneth over them. {Job 34:30} Such a one was Zedekiah; and the prophet here freely reproveth him for his hypocrisy.
paragraphs.anchor: If I declare it unto thee.

paragraphs.text: Or, And though I advise thee, thou wilt not hearken to me. Thou art set, and hast made thy conclusion beforehand.
paragraphs.anchor: And if I give thee counsel, will thou not hearken?

paragraphs.text: But what credit was to be given to his oath, who was notoriously known to be a perjured person, as having broken his oath of fidelity to Nebuchadnezzar?
paragraphs.anchor: So the king Zedekiah sware secretly unto Jeremiah.

paragraphs.text: Hence the truth of that assertion is cleared up unto us, that men’s souls drop not down from heaven, nor are propagated by their parents, but are created by God, and infused into their bodies.
paragraphs.anchor: As the Lord liveth, that made us this soul.

paragraphs.text: The former part of the prophet’s condition he sweareth to perform, but saith nothing to the latter, as having no such liking to it. So many come today to hear, who resolve to practise only so far as they see good.
paragraphs.anchor: I will not put thee to death, neither will I, &c.

paragraphs.text: Jeremiah was semper idem, one and the same still; no changeling at all, but a faithful and constant preacher of God’s Word.
paragraphs.anchor: If thou wilt assuredly go forth.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 32:39. Thus Zedekiah hath it both ways, that it may abide by him; but he was uncounselable and irreclaimable.
paragraphs.anchor: But if thou wilt not go forth.

paragraphs.text: Thus hypocrites will at one time or other detect themselves, as Zedekiah here plainly declareth that he more feared the loss of his life, honour, wealth, &c., than of God’s favour and kingdom; so do the most among us. Pilate feared how Caesar would take it if he should release Jesus. Herod laid hold on Peter, after he had killed James, that he might please the people. The Pharisees could not believe, because they received glory from men. This generous king cannot endure to think that his own fugitives should flout him; but to be ruled by God, and his holy prophet advising him for the best, he cannot yield. Thus still vain men are niggardly of their reputation and prodigal of their souls. Do we not see them run wilfully into the field, into the grave, into hell? and all lest it should be said they have as much fear as wit.
paragraphs.anchor: Then Zedekiah said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews.

paragraphs.text: This the good prophet speaketh from the mouth of the Lord, to cure him of that causeless fear, and to bring him to a better obedience; but it was past time of day with him to be wrought upon by anything that could be spoken, though never so well.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not deliver thee.

paragraphs.text: This is also the voice of the gospel, and the result of all the promises.
paragraphs.anchor: So it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.

paragraphs.text: Promises and threatenings make an excellent mixture; the tartness of the one giveth us better to taste the sweetness of the other.
paragraphs.anchor: Bat if thou refuse to go forth.

paragraphs.text: These shall mock thee and make songs of thee, exagitantes regem socordissimum, for a simple and sorry man, who hath undone them altogether with himself, by listening to flatterers and false prophets.
paragraphs.anchor: And, behold, all the women that are left.

paragraphs.text: In the mire of misery, where the prophet’s unworthy usage in the miry dungeon is hinted, and the king twitted with it, as some hold. Some again think that Zedekiah in his flight did run into some quagmire, where he was taken.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy feet are sunk in the mire.

paragraphs.text: Thy flatterers have now left thee in the lurch.
paragraphs.anchor: And they are turned away backward.

paragraphs.text: Or, Thy women (whether wives or concubines, that crew of wanton creatures) and thy sons; for his daughters were left behind. {Jer 41:10; Jer 43:6} If, therefore, thou hast any care of those that are, or ought to be, most dear unto thee, be ruled by me.
paragraphs.anchor: So shall they bring out all thy wives and thy children.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Thou shalt burn this city:
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt cause this city to be burnt with fire.

paragraphs.text: “ Quicquid delirant reges, plectuntur Achivi. ”
Muliebriter deprecatur rex incredulus fidelem. Thus he who feareth not God, feareth his own servants and counsellors.
paragraphs.anchor: Let no man know of these words

paragraphs.text: The crafty king would seem to be solicitous of the prophet’s safety, but mainly intendeth his own.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt not die.

paragraphs.text: In such fear stood he of his princes, and might truly say, as the Assyrian once did, Are not my princes altogether kings? {Isa 10:8} or as the Emperor of Germany did, I am king of kings, meaning that the princes of his empire would do what they wished for all him. Zedekiah was only an image of a king.
paragraphs.anchor: But if the princes hear.

paragraphs.text: This was to tell part of the truth only (which might lawfully be done), and not to tell an officious, or at least an oblique lie, as some would make it to be.
paragraphs.anchor: Then shalt thou say unto them, I presented my supplication.

paragraphs.text: Indigni utique qui ultra monerentur. The princes were far worse than the king, {a} who yet himself was one of the best. They therefore were slain by the Babylonian princes, when the king’s life was preserved, though with the loss of his eyes, which yet might be a means to open the eyes of his mind.
paragraphs.anchor: So they left off speaking with him.

paragraphs.text: {a} In una impietate solum stabiles.

Which now God had made to him a sanctuary of safety, and a very Bethlehem, or house of bread. God can easily turn a prison into a paradise, and brown bread and water into manchet and wine, as he did to the martyrs. One of them dated his letter thus, From the delectable orchard of the Leonine prison.
paragraphs.anchor: So Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison.
